subject: Adding lines to a discrete/continuous plot

messages.author: c91a208fffacfb7e
messages.subject: Adding lines to a discrete/continuous plot
parts:
I want to create an interaction plot including the original data.
Some sample data can be obtained as

DataURL <- "http://www.stat.wisc.edu/~st849-1/data/"
str(hayfever <- within(read.table(paste(DataURL, "hayfever.txt", sep=""),
header = TRUE),
{
A <- factor(A)
B <- factor(B)
id <- factor(id)
}))

and my attempt to create the plot, based on the examples in the
documentation for stat_summary, is

qplot(A, hours, data=hayfever) + aes(color=B) +
stat_summary(fun.y=mean, geom="line")

but I don't get the lines on the plot, apparently because A is
discrete. If I make the x-axis numeric, as in

hayfever$a <- as.integer(as.character(hayfever$A))
qplot(a, hours, data=hayfever) + aes(color=B) +
stat_summary(fun.y=mean, geom="line")

then I get the lines. Is there a way to obtain the lines without
changing A from a factor to numeric?

messages.author: 936ef8c6d12fc338
messages.subject: RE: Adding lines to a discrete/continuous plot
parts:
Dear Douglas,

You need to add group = B to the aesthetics.

library(ggplot2)

DataURL <- "http://www.stat.wisc.edu/~st849-1/data/"
str(hayfever <- within(read.table(paste(DataURL, "hayfever.txt", sep=""),
                                                header = TRUE),
                                {
                                        A <- factor(A)
                                        B <- factor(B)
                                        id <- factor(id)
                                }))

ggplot(hayfever, aes(x = A, y = hours, colour = B, group = B)) + stat_summary(fun.y=mean, geom="line")

Best regards,

Thierry

messages.author: 66a7bbbceef834e9
messages.subject: Re: Adding lines to a discrete/continuous plot
parts:
Douglas, you just have change add the grouping variable to your code:

qplot(A, hours, data=hayfever) + aes(color=B, group = B) +
stat_summary(fun.y=mean, geom="line")

HTH

Luciano

messages.subject: Re: Adding lines to a discrete/continuous plot
parts:
My students had need of much the same thing this summer and I wrote a
function for it. I'm attaching one example of a plot that can be done. The
function and some test data/examples are also attached since they are
longish. You would also need the ChemoSpec package at
http://github.com/bryanhanson/ChemoSpec for the functions used in
stat_summary.

If the plot is along the lines of what you want to do then hack away at
these files to your heart's content. There's lots of control built in -
show/don't show raw data, summary table or not, type of summary stat.

Bryan
